title: Practice: bind a generator for a rare value
vision: Give a law the valid ISBNs it needs when random numbers almost never carry the right check digit, and see the law exercised with them.
explanation: Laws and generation strategies are authored in LawSpec. Only the implementation changes language.
news: A law over a restricted type needs a valid value to test; a generator or an example supplies it.
contributions: A catalogued-book loan law refused for lack of a valid ISBN, repaired once with an example and once with a generator that computes the check digit. The generator exposes a 14-day bug on real ISBNs; every value is checked against the restriction. Evidence covers the ISBNs the generator draws, with renewal counts from 0 to 5.

star.salient: A law over a restricted type needs a value of that type, and a generator can build one every run.
star.surprise: A law can compile and pass while never meeting the case it names; LawSpec refuses it instead.
star.story: The library catalogues books by ISBN-13, whose last digit is a check digit. Random numbers almost never carry the right one, so without a valid ISBN the loan law proves nothing; a generator that computes the check digit exercises it every run and finds the 14-day bug.

hints: Which request would show that a catalogued book gets 14 days? Find the ISBN in the failing input.
Compare loanDays 0 with the 28 the law demands. What constant should the formula start from?
Start from 28 and add 7 for each renewal. Load solution shows the complete repair.

stages.title: The law has no valid ISBN to test
story: The library gives a catalogued book a long loan: at least 28 days when a request has at most three renewals. A catalogued book is known by its ISBN-13, thirteen digits that start 978 or 979. The last digit is a check digit: weight the first twelve digits 1, 3, 1, 3 and so on, and the check digit brings the total up to a multiple of ten. About one thirteen-digit number in ten has the right one.

The law is “for all requests” (a book and a renewal count), and nothing in Tests.lawspec or the harness shows an ISBN that passes. Predict what Run checks does, then run it. Without a valid ISBN the law could only ever check other cases, and it would look as if it passed.

LawSpec does not let that happen. Once the compiler can show a value neither by its boundary search nor from the law’s examples nor from 1000 sampled values, it refuses the law, with the message: “no value of Isbn found by the boundary search or in 1000 sampled values”. It then tells the author to give the law an example whose input holds an ISBN, or to bind a generator for the input. The next two steps do each.

run.refusal: no value of Isbn found by the boundary search or in 1000 sampled values, so no case of this law could hold one. Give the law an example whose input holds one, or bind a generator.

stages.action: Run all checks and read the refusal. Explain in your own words what the law would have checked if it had been allowed to pass.
stages.reason: A claim that is never exercised on its restricted input is not evidence. A refusal keeps that visible; a silent pass hides it.
stages.expect: The compiler refuses the law and no checks run. Read the diagnostic: it names the type that has no value.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: wrapper Isbn is Integer where … end wrapper declares a restricted type: a number that fails the restriction is not an Isbn. Its restriction says the last digit must equal checkDigitFor the first twelve. A record field of that type means every Request holds a valid ISBN.
harnessNotes: This harness only names the law. It supplies no strategy, so the compiler must find an ISBN on its own, and it cannot.
A harness changes which inputs are tried, not what the law claims. The next steps change Tests or the Harness so that a valid ISBN exists.
stages.symbol: 9780306406157 is an ISBN; most 13-digit numbers are not

stages.title: Fix A: show the law one ISBN
story: The smallest repair is an example: a concrete input for the law. 9780306406157 is a real ISBN-13: its first twelve digits weigh 93, and a check digit of 7 brings the total to 100. The law now has an example whose input holds an ISBN, so the compiler has a value to work from.

That is enough to lift the refusal, but it is one ISBN. The law is still exercised on a single value of the restricted type. Run the checks and see that the starter, which gives only 14 days, fails the example.
stages.action: Read the example, run all checks and find the ISBN in the failing input.
stages.reason: An example is the quickest way to give a law a witness, and it also documents one valid value. It does not vary.
stages.expect: The compiler accepts the law because its example holds an ISBN, then the 14-day starter fails the law on that ISBN.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: example "|…| : request = Request record{ book = Isbn 9780306406157 , renewals = 0 } expect … end example binds the quantified input request, then states what must hold. Isbn 9780306406157 builds an ISBN; a number with the wrong check digit is rejected.
harnessNotes: The harness is unchanged: still no strategy. The example, not the harness, supplied the ISBN.

stages.title: Fix B: bind a generator that computes the check digit
story: The main repair is a generator: a recipe that builds valid ISBNs so that every run draws them. The example is gone from Tests.lawspec; the Harness now declares strategy bodies, isbns and requests, and binds the law to requests with use requests for request.

A generator is the right tool when valid values follow a rule you can compute. Here the first twelve digits can be anything that starts 978 or 979, and the check digit follows from them. The strategy draws twelve digits as the number body, then builds Isbn (body * 10 + checkDigitFor body): the same checkDigitFor the restriction uses. The compiler no longer needs to search, and the law is exercised with those ISBNs on every run, with renewal counts from 0 to 5.

A found or generated value is always checked against the restriction, so a strategy that built a wrong check digit would be caught instead of silently trusted. Run all checks: the law now meets real ISBNs, and the 14-day starter fails it, with the failing request shown.
stages.action: Open the Harness tab, read bodies, isbns and requests, then run all checks and read the failing request.
stages.reason: Binding a generator makes valid values part of every run, so the law keeps exercising the case that the restriction makes rare.
stages.expect: The law is accepted and exercised, and the starter fails it on a request whose book is a generated ISBN.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: strategy name :: T is … end strategy declares a recipe. bind x :: S from g in … draws x from g and uses it below. one of e builds the value e. for law "|…| use requests for request end for law connects the strategy to the law’s quantified input.
harnessNotes: bodies draws a twelve-digit number from 978000000000 through 979999999999, so every ISBN starts 978 or 979. isbns binds one such body, then builds the ISBN by putting the check digit that checkDigitFor works out after it.

requests combines a book from isbns with a renewal count from 0 through 5. The count is wider than the law’s 0 to 3 on purpose: the law’s own guard decides which cases it speaks about, not the strategy.

The binding for “a request for a catalogued book gets the long loan” selects the claim in Laws; use requests for request supplies the quantified input request. The generator does not provide the expected answer, and a drawn value is checked against the Isbn restriction before the law sees it.

stages.title: Repair the loan and keep the generator
story: The failing request is real: a request for a catalogued book with no renewals gets 14 days, not at least 28. Change loanDays so such a request gets 28 days plus 7 for each renewal, then run all checks again.

As your own challenge, change the isbns strategy in the Harness to build body * 10 + checkDigitFor body + 1 and predict what the run does. That ISBN has a wrong check digit. The run reports “field refinement 1 failed” for Isbn: the value is checked against the restriction instead of being trusted.
stages.action: Repair loanDays and run all checks. Then break the generator’s check digit as described and read what the run reports.
stages.reason: The generator exposes the bug and then keeps guarding the repair: every run draws ISBNs.
stages.expect: The supplied starter fails the generated law. After the repair, the same run passes; with the wrong check digit the run stops with “field refinement 1 failed” for Isbn.
stages.recovery: Reset this step restores its supplied files and seed. After an edit, use the actual result to judge your version; the story’s prediction describes the supplied files.
stages.syntax: The law needs the result to be at least 28 for 0 through 3 renewals. A formula that starts at 28 and adds 7 per renewal satisfies it.

implementationSyntax.fsharp: In F#, loanDays takes the renewal count as an int and returns an int. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.
implementationSyntax.typescript: In TypeScript, number is the argument and result type. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.
implementationSyntax.javascript: In JavaScript, the function takes the renewal count and returns a number. 14 + 7 * renewals gives 14 days for none; the repair starts from 28.

naming: Use English phrase names for readable claims and descriptive LawSpec helpers. Keep short code names such as add, sort, xs and numbers when they make calls and recipes easier to follow. A phrase starts with "| and ends with |, without a closing quote. A law label identifies the claim; renaming it does not change what the definition checks. The compiler generates target-appropriate names.
